name: Rice
origin: Yangtze River Valley, China (domesticated ~9,000 years ago)
description: Rice is a semi-aquatic cereal grain that feeds more than half of the global population. In river deltas like the Mekong, flooded paddies suppress weeds and buffer root temperatures.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Pre-soaked seeds imbibe water and germinate in saturated nursery beds.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Coleoptile and primary leaves emerge; seedlings are transplanted into flooded paddies.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Rapid tillering builds stems and dense green canopy.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Panicles emerge and pollinate; stable warm temperatures are critical.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Grains fill and turn golden; paddies drain before cutting.

idealConditions.soilType: Alluvial clay or silty clay loam (low permeability)

funFacts: Rice paddies host nitrogen-fixing Azolla ferns that naturally fertilize the crop.
Specialized air channels called aerenchyma pipe oxygen down to submerged roots.
Over 120,000 distinct cultivated varieties of rice exist worldwide.
nutritionHighlights: Rich source of complex carbohydrates, manganese, selenium, and B vitamins (especially in brown rice).
nasaMonitoring: MODIS and Landsat NDVI track paddy greenness and flood timing, while GPM IMERG monitors monsoon rainfall and SMAP tracks delta moisture.

name: Winter Wheat
origin: Fertile Crescent, Western Asia (~10,000 years ago)
description: Winter wheat is planted in autumn, enters dormancy beneath winter snow, and surges into growth in spring. It anchors global bread production and thrives in temperate grasslands.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Drilled into cool autumn soil; germinates rapidly with light moisture.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Autumn leaves form a rosette and vernalize through winter freeze.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Spring jointing lifts nodes upward as stems elongate.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Spikes emerge and self-pollinate under mild spring sun.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Amber grain dries down to ~13% moisture for combine harvest.

idealConditions.soilType: Deep silt loam or clay loam

funFacts: Winter wheat requires a cold chill period called vernalization before it can flower.
A single wheat head typically holds 40 to 60 kernels arranged in spikelets.
Wheat covers more cultivated land area globally than any other food crop.

benefits.shade: Low crop canopy shades topsoil surface by late spring, lowering soil moisture loss.
benefits.soilHealth: Dense fibrous root mat anchors topsoil through winter wind and rain.
benefits.pollinators: Wind-pollinated grass; undisturbed straw margins shelter ground beetles.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~2,200 kg CO₂/ha captured in seasonal grain and straw biomass

nutritionHighlights: Provides dietary fiber, plant protein (gluten), iron, zinc, and B-complex vitamins.
nasaMonitoring: NASA Harvest uses MODIS, Landsat 8/9, and SMAP soil moisture anomalies to forecast regional wheat yields months before harvest.

name: Maize (Corn)
origin: Balsas River Valley, Mexico (~9,000 years ago)
description: Maize is a high-efficiency C4 grass domesticated from wild teosinte. It converts intense summer sunlight and deep prairie moisture into tall stalks and dense ears of grain.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Planted once soil temperatures exceed 10°C in spring.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: V2–V4 leaf collars emerge and anchor nodal roots.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Rapid stem elongation reaches 2–3 meters height.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Tassels shed pollen onto silks; heat >35°C stresses pollination.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Kernels dent and dry down to golden physiological maturity.

idealConditions.soilType: Fertile, well-drained prairie loam

funFacts: Every kernel on a corn cob is connected to its own individual strand of corn silk.
An ear of maize almost always has an even number of kernel rows (commonly 16).
As a C4 plant, maize captures carbon twice as efficiently in bright sun as wheat.

benefits.shade: Tall 2.5 m stalks act as living trellises and summer windbreaks for understory squash.
benefits.soilHealth: Deep brace and fibrous roots improve subsoil aeration when rotated with legumes.
benefits.pollinators: Tassels offer abundant late-summer pollen gathered by honeybees.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~3,800 kg CO₂/ha seasonal biomass uptake (C4 photosynthesis)

nutritionHighlights: Rich in carotenoids (lutein and zeaxanthin), vitamin C, magnesium, and energy-dense starch.
nasaMonitoring: Landsat 8/9 thermal bands detect canopy water stress during silking, while POWER solar radiation models biomass growth.

name: Arabica Coffee
description: Arabica coffee thrives on cool tropical hillsides between 800 and 1,800 meters elevation. Gentle rainfall cycles trigger synchronized white blossoms followed by crimson cherries.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Parchment seeds germinate slowly in shaded nursery soil.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Cotyledon 'soldier' leaves unfurl into glossy paired foliage.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Woody branching canopy establishes root depth.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Fragrant white jasmine-like blossoms open for 2–3 days.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Green berries ripen into deep red cherries ready for picking.

idealConditions.soilType: Volcanic or deep well-drained lateritic loam

funFacts: Coffee beans are actually the paired seeds inside a sweet red fruit called a coffee cherry.
Arabica is extremely sensitive to frost—a single freezing night can damage years of yield.
Shade-grown coffee plantations double as vital migratory bird habitats.
nutritionHighlights: Contains natural antioxidants (chlorogenic acids), polyphenols, potassium, and caffeine.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER frost and heat-stress tracking helps highland growers protect blooms, while MODIS monitors dry-season stress.

name: Cacao (Cocoa)
description: Cacao is an understory rainforest tree whose pods sprout directly from the trunk and main branches (cauliflory). It demands steady warmth, high humidity, and dappled shade.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Fresh seeds have no dormancy and must be planted immediately.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Young stems push upward with bronze-tinted flush leaves.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Jorquette branching forms a broad shaded canopy.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Tiny flowers grow on bark and are pollinated by biting midges.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Ribbed pods turn golden-orange with 30–50 beans inside.

idealConditions.soilType: Deep, humus-rich clay loam

funFacts: The scientific name Theobroma literally translates to 'Food of the Gods'.
Cacao flowers are pollinated almost exclusively by tiny midges smaller than a pinhead.
Raw cacao beans undergo a 5–7 day microbial fermentation before tasting like chocolate.
nutritionHighlights: Packed with flavanols, magnesium, iron, copper, and theobromine.
nasaMonitoring: GPM rainfall anomalies and SMAP topsoil moisture reveal Harmattan drought stress across West African cocoa belts.

name: Assam Tea
description: Tea is a resilient evergreen camellia shrub pruned into waist-high plucking tables. Warm humid valleys like Assam produce rapid, malty flushes of tender two-leaf-and-a-bud shoots.

growthStages.label: Seed / Cutting
growthStages.summary: Vegetative nodal cuttings root in misted acidic nursery beds.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: First axillary shoots emerge with fine silvery hairs.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: New tender green shoots cycle every 7–14 days during rains.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Small white blossoms appear if bushes are left unpruned.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Top two leaves and unopened bud are hand-plucked.

idealConditions.soilType: Deep, well-drained acidic sandy loam

funFacts: Green, black, oolong, and white tea all come from the exact same plant species—only processing differs.
Tea thrives in strongly acidic soil (pH 4.5–5.5) where most other crops struggle.
Morning dew and misty valley clouds protect tender tea buds from scorching midday UV.
nutritionHighlights: Rich in catechins (EGCG), L-theanine amino acids, polyphenols, and fluoride.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER humidity and solar irradiance track flush cadence, while EONET and GPM alert river-valley estates to flood peaks.

name: Upland Cotton
description: Cotton is a sun-loving perennial shrub grown as an annual for its pure cellulose seed fibers. It thrives in hot, arid river basins where dry autumn weather keeps mature bolls clean.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Seeds germinate rapidly in warm soils above 18°C.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Taproot dives deep while broad heart-shaped cotyledons open.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Woody main stem branches out and forms fruiting 'squares'.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Cream flowers turn pink after pollination and swell into bolls.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Bolls crack open to reveal fluffy white lint fibers.

idealConditions.soilType: Deep alluvial loam or sandy clay loam

funFacts: Each cotton fiber is a single elongated plant cell made of nearly 95% pure cellulose.
Cotton blossoms naturally change color from creamy white to rose pink within 24 hours of pollination.
Cottonseed also produces edible cooking oil and high-protein livestock feed.
nutritionHighlights: Non-food fiber crop; refined cottonseed oil provides vitamin E and unsaturated fatty acids.
nasaMonitoring: Landsat thermal imagery quantifies irrigation demand in the Indus Basin, while POWER heatwaves warn of boll shedding above 40°C.

name: Sugarcane
description: Sugarcane is a giant tropical C4 grass storing sucrose inside thick fibrous stalks. Warm wet summers build tall biomass, followed by a cooler dry spell that concentrates sugar before harvest.

growthStages.label: Sett Planting
growthStages.summary: Stem cuttings ('setts') with buds sprout from underground nodes.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Shoots emerge and begin heavy tillering into clumps.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Grand growth phase builds 3–4 meter canes during summer rains.

growthStages.label: Ripening
growthStages.summary: Cooler dry weather slows growth and packs stalks with sucrose.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Stalks are cut cleanly at ground level; ratoon shoots regrow.

idealConditions.soilType: Deep, well-structured clay loam or red latosol

funFacts: Sugarcane is the world's largest crop by total harvested tonnage (~1.9 billion tons/year).
Crushed cane fiber (bagasse) powers sugar mills and generates renewable bioelectricity.
Once planted, sugarcane regrows up to 4–6 successive 'ratoon' harvests from the same roots.
nutritionHighlights: Primary source of natural sucrose; unrefined cane juice contains potassium, calcium, and iron.
nasaMonitoring: MODIS NDVI and NASA POWER solar radiation track grand-growth vigor and dry-down ripening across São Paulo estates.

name: Olive
description: The olive is a drought-hardy Mediterranean evergreen tree with silvery-green leaves that reflect harsh sun. Mild wet winters and hot dry summers produce oil-rich drupes.

growthStages.label: Propagation
growthStages.summary: Rooted hardwood cuttings establish in rocky limestone soil.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Silvery new shoots and flower panicles bud after winter chill.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Deep roots tap subsoil moisture while stone pits harden.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Wind pollinates clusters of creamy-white four-petaled blooms.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Green olives darken to purple-black as oil peaks inside.

idealConditions.soilType: Well-drained calcareous rocky loam

funFacts: Individual olive trees can live and bear fruit for over 1,500 years.
Silvery hairs on the underside of olive leaves reduce water evaporation in summer heat.
Jaén, Spain alone hosts more than 66 million olive trees visible from orbit.
nutritionHighlights: Extra-virgin olive oil is rich in heart-healthy oleic acid (monounsaturated fat), vitamin E, and polyphenols.
nasaMonitoring: SMAP soil moisture and MODIS land-surface temperature track Mediterranean heatwaves and deficit irrigation needs.

name: Andean Potato
origin: High Andes of Peru & Bolivia (~8,000 years ago)
description: Domesticated at 3,800 meters near Lake Titicaca, potatoes thrive in cool mountain air and crisp sunlight. Underground tubers swell rapidly when night temperatures drop below 15°C.

growthStages.label: Seed Tuber
growthStages.summary: Sprouted 'eyes' on planted seed tubers send roots into loose soil.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Leafy green stems break the ridge and begin photosynthesis.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Underground stolons swell into baby tubers during hilling.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Violet or white star-shaped flowers signal peak tuber bulking.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Foliage senesces and tuber skins set firm for digging.

idealConditions.soilType: Loose, friable sandy loam or volcanic silt

funFacts: More than 4,000 native potato varieties are cultivated in the Peruvian Andes.
Cool nights are essential—warm nights above 22°C halt underground tuber formation.
Potatoes were the first food crop ever grown experimentally in space aboard Space Shuttle Columbia (1995).
nutritionHighlights: Excellent source of vitamin C, potassium (more than a banana), vitamin B6, and resistant starch.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER minimum-temperature series flag Andean frost hazards, while GIBS snow/cloud products help time planting.

name: Soybean
description: Soybean is a protein-rich legume that partners with Rhizobium root bacteria to pull nitrogen straight out of the air, enriching the soil for subsequent crops like maize or cotton.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Round seeds absorb twice their weight in water to germinate.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Unifoliate and trifoliate leaves open while root nodules form.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Bushy canopy closes rows to shade out weeds.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Tiny purple or white blossoms develop clusters of fuzzy pods.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Leaves yellow and drop; dry pods rattle cleanly for harvest.

idealConditions.soilType: Well-drained loam or savanna oxisol (limed)
idealConditions.growingSeason: Wet warm summer (Oct–Feb in Mato Grosso)

funFacts: Soybeans contain ~38–40% protein by weight—double most other beans.
Symbiotic Rhizobium nodules on soybean roots naturally fix 100+ kg of nitrogen per hectare.
Soybean planting in Mato Grosso is frequently double-cropped with maize in the same year.
nutritionHighlights: Complete plant protein containing all nine essential amino acids, plus isoflavones, iron, and folate.
nasaMonitoring: MODIS and Landsat track Cerrado double-cropping transitions, while GPM IMERG tracks onset of the South American monsoon.

name: Date Palm
description: The date palm is an iconic desert oasis crop famous for the saying 'its feet in water and its head in the fire of the sky.' Intense dry summer heat ripens sweet dates high above irrigated groves.

growthStages.label: Offshoot
growthStages.summary: Clonal offshoots are planted beside oasis irrigation channels.

growthStages.label: Crown Flush
growthStages.summary: Feathery pinnate fronds fan out from a sturdy fibrous trunk.

growthStages.label: Canopy
growthStages.summary: Mature palms shade cooler understory citrus and vegetable beds.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Male pollen strands dust female flower spathes high in the crown.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Heavy golden-amber date bunches ripen in arid heat.

idealConditions.soilType: Deep sandy loam (tolerates mild salinity)

funFacts: Date palms are dioecious—growers plant separate male and female trees and hand-pollinate crowns.
Al-Ahsa Oasis hosts over 2.5 million date palms fed by natural artesian springs.
A single mature palm can yield over 100 kg of nutrient-dense dates every autumn.
nutritionHighlights: Rich in natural fruit sugars, potassium, magnesium, dietary fiber, and polyphenols.
nasaMonitoring: Landsat thermal and MODIS albedo monitor oasis oasis-cooling microclimates and aquifer irrigation health.

name: Sunflowers
description: Sunflowers lift bright golden flower heads that track the morning sun (heliotropism) before locking eastward to warm bees at dawn. Deep taproots pull up subsoil nutrients and resist summer dry spells.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Striped achenes germinate rapidly in spring soils warmed above 10°C.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Broad cotyledons unfold as the taproot anchors deep.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Sturdy hairy stems surge upward and follow the sun east-to-west.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Thousands of central disc florets open in Fibonacci spirals for bees.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Flower backs turn lemon-yellow to brown as oil-rich seeds mature.

idealConditions.soilType: Well-drained sandy loam or prairie loam

funFacts: Young sunflower buds physically turn from east to west every day following an internal circadian clock.
Every sunflower head is actually a composite of up to 2,000 tiny individual florets.
Mature heads stay facing east because morning sun warms bees 5x faster than west-facing blooms.

benefits.shade: Broad overlapping leaves cool fence-line soil and suppress annual weeds.
benefits.soilHealth: Taproots reach 1.5–2 m deep, mining potassium and opening compacted plow pans.
benefits.pollinators: High-value nectar and pollen beacon for honeybees, bumblebees, and hoverflies.

nutritionHighlights: Rich in vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol), selenium, magnesium, and heart-healthy polyunsaturated fats.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER solar irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN) predicts oil content and seed-fill rates, while MODIS NDVI maps peak golden bloom.

name: Heirloom Tomatoes
origin: Andean slopes of Peru & Ecuador; domesticated in Mesoamerica
description: Sun-ripened tomatoes convert warm days and cool nights into balanced sugars and organic acids. Consistent soil moisture prevents blossom-end rot and cracking while fruiting.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Tiny fuzzy seeds sprout indoors at 22–26°C before last spring frost.

growthStages.label: Transplant
growthStages.summary: Seedlings harden off and plant deep so stems sprout extra roots.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Trellised vines build compound leaves and strong fruiting trusses.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Yellow buzz-pollinated blossoms set fruit best when nights stay 15–21°C.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Fruits blush from green to crimson as lycopene pigments peak.

idealConditions.soilType: Rich, well-drained composted loam

funFacts: Tomato flowers require 'buzz pollination'—bumblebees vibrate their flight muscles at ~400 Hz to release pollen.
Tomatoes were once feared in 18th-century Europe because lead pewter plates leached toxins in acidic tomato juice.
Burying two-thirds of a tomato stem at planting triggers adventitious roots along the entire stem.

benefits.shade: Staked vines shade soil beds beneath, preserving evening soil moisture.
benefits.soilHealth: Benefits strongly from crop rotation with legumes and deep straw mulching.
benefits.pollinators: Draws native bumblebees when interplanted beside basil, marigolds, and lavender.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~1,650 kg CO₂/ha captured in high-yield vine biomass

nutritionHighlights: Loaded with lycopene antioxidants, vitamin C, potassium, folate, and vitamin K.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER night minimum temperatures (T2M_MIN) alert growers to frost or heat-induced blossom drop, while SMAP tracks root-zone moisture.

name: Farm Pumpkins
description: Running pumpkin vines blanket warm sunny soil under broad prickly leaves that act as living mulch. Part of the traditional Indigenous 'Three Sisters' polyculture alongside corn and beans.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Large flat seeds sprout once soil holds steady above 18°C.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Broad paddle cotyledons fuel rapid vine runner emergence.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Trailing vines anchor secondary roots along leaf nodes.

growthStages.label: Flowering
growthStages.summary: Large golden trumpet blooms open at dawn for specialist squash bees.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Rinds harden into deep orange as stems turn corky.

idealConditions.soilType: Fertile, moisture-retentive sandy or silt loam

funFacts: Native squash bees (Peponapis pruinosa) sleep inside closed pumpkin blossoms overnight.
Pumpkins are roughly 90% water yet cure for 3–6 months in cool barns.
The largest recorded pumpkin topped 1,246 kg (2,749 lbs)—growing over 20 kg per day in peak summer.

benefits.shade: Huge umbrella leaves shade topsoil, suppressing weeds and cooling roots for corn companion crops.
benefits.soilHealth: Cuts evaporation and prevents splash erosion during late-summer thunderstorms.
benefits.pollinators: Dawn-blooming trumpets sustain solitary native squash bees and honeybees.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~2,100 kg CO₂/ha captured in sprawling seasonal vines

nutritionHighlights: Rich in beta-carotene (provitamin A), potassium, fiber, vitamin E, and zinc-rich seeds.
nasaMonitoring: GPM IMERG rainfall accumulation and NASA POWER humidity (RH2M) help growers anticipate powdery mildew windows.

name: Honeycrisp Apple Tree
origin: Tian Shan mountains of Kazakhstan (~4,000–10,000 years ago)
description: Orchard apple trees thrive on gentle valley slopes where cold winter chill hours break dormancy and spring frost drains downhill. Cool autumn nights concentrate crisp fruit sugars.

growthStages.label: Dormant Bud
growthStages.summary: Requires 800–1,000 winter chill hours (0–7°C) to reset spring flower buds.

growthStages.label: Bud Break
growthStages.summary: Silver-tip buds swell into emerald leaf clusters ('tight cluster').

growthStages.label: Canopy
growthStages.summary: Deep woody branches expand photosynthetic crown for fruit fill.

growthStages.label: Blossom
growthStages.summary: Fragrant pink-white blossoms require cross-pollination by orchard bees.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Crisp apples color bright crimson as autumn nights turn cool.

idealConditions.soilType: Well-drained gravelly or silt loam on sloped terrain
idealConditions.daysToHarvest: 3–5 years to first harvest (140 days bloom-to-pick)

funFacts: Apple trees are not true-to-seed—every orchard Honeycrisp or Granny Smith is grafted from a single original tree.
Crisp autumn nights below 10°C trigger red anthocyanin pigments and sweeter fruit crunch.
An orchard needs at least two different apple varieties blooming nearby for bee cross-pollination.

benefits.shade: Spreading orchard crown cools pasture edges and shelters beneficial birds.
benefits.soilHealth: Perennial woody roots stabilize hillsides and host rich mycorrhizal fungal webs.
benefits.pollinators: Spring orchard blossoms are an essential early-season feast for mason bees and honeybees.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~22 kg CO₂/tree/yr stored in woody trunk and roots

treeDetails.height: 4–7 m (semi-dwarf orchard) / up to 10 m standard
treeDetails.leafShape: Simple oval serrated leaves with downy undersides

nutritionHighlights: Rich in soluble pectin fiber, quercetin antioxidants (concentrated in the peel), and vitamin C.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER minimum temperatures track lethal spring blossom frosts, while MODIS EVI maps seasonal leaf-out timing.

name: English Lavender
description: Aromatic woody perennial sub-shrub prized for violet flower spikes and fragrant essential oils. Thrives in full sun, brisk breezes, and lean, gritty, sharply drained soils.

growthStages.label: Cutting / Seed
growthStages.summary: Softwood cuttings or cold-stratified seeds establish in sandy pots.

growthStages.label: Rooting
growthStages.summary: Silvery-grey aromatic shoots form a compact evergreen mound.

growthStages.label: Vegetative
growthStages.summary: Silvery foliage thickens without excess nitrogen or wet feet.

growthStages.label: Bloom
growthStages.summary: Whorled violet spikes rise above leaves, humming with bees.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Cut just as half the florets open for peak linalool essential oil.

idealConditions.soilType: Gravelly, sandy, alkaline well-drained loam
idealConditions.daysToHarvest: 90–120 days from spring growth (Year 2+ full yield)

funFacts: Lavandula comes from the Latin 'lavare' (to wash)—Romans scented baths and linens with dried spikes.
Silvery hairs on lavender leaves reflect harsh summer sunlight and trap humid air around stomata.
Rainy, overly humid clay soils are lavender's main enemy; gravel mulch keeps crowns dry.
uses: Dried fragrant bundles & natural moth repellent

benefits.shade: Low silver mounds keep topsoil cool while allowing airflow between rows.
benefits.soilHealth: Deep fibrous roots bind stony slopes with minimal irrigation or fertilizer.
benefits.pollinators: Magnet for bumblebees, honeybees, and painted lady butterflies all summer.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~950 kg CO₂/ha steady woody perennial sequestration

nutritionHighlights: Aromatic terpenes (linalool and linalyl acetate) valued in herbal teas and soothing aromatherapy.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER precipitation and RH2M humidity highlight root-rot risk periods, while solar flux correlates with essential oil yield.

name: Nantes Carrot Rows
origin: Afghan plateau & Central Asia (~1,100+ years ago)
description: Crisp sweet biennial root vegetable grown as an annual in stone-free sandy loam. Cool autumn evenings convert root starches into sugars for sweet flavor.

growthStages.label: Seed
growthStages.summary: Tiny slow-sprouting seeds need steady surface dampness to germinate.

growthStages.label: Sprout
growthStages.summary: Thread-like grass cotyledons give way to feathery fern-like true leaves.

growthStages.label: Root Lengthening
growthStages.summary: Fine taproot dives downward before swelling outward.

growthStages.label: Bulking
growthStages.summary: Orange carotene concentrates inside crisp cylindrical storage roots.

growthStages.label: Harvest
growthStages.summary: Sweet, bright orange roots are lifted from loose damp beds.

idealConditions.soilType: Deep, stone-free sandy loam or peat

funFacts: Original domesticated carrots in Central Asia were purple and yellow—orange varieties became widespread in the 17th-century Netherlands.
Even a light frost sweetens carrots in the ground as plants convert starches into antifreeze sugars.
Carrots belong to the same family as dill, parsley, fennel, and wild Queen Anne's lace.
uses: Soups, stews, and roasted root medleys

benefits.shade: Feathery dense foliage shades bed soil against crusting between irrigations.
benefits.soilHealth: Loosens topsoil channels and makes an ideal follow-on crop after heavy compost crops.
benefits.pollinators: Second-year umbel flowers attract parasitic wasps and hoverflies that eat garden aphids.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~1,400 kg CO₂/ha seasonal root and top uptake

nutritionHighlights: Exceptionally high in beta-carotene (vitamin A for vision), biotin, potassium, and fiber.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER soil-warming averages guide early spring sowing, while SMAP topsoil moisture ensures uniform germination without splitting.

name: White Oak
description: A majestic keystone broadleaf tree framing the farmhouse edge. Its wide spreading crown cools farm buildings in summer and supports more native caterpillar and bird species than almost any other tree.

growthStages.label: Acorn
growthStages.summary: Sweet white oak acorns sprout a taproot immediately in autumn leaf litter.

growthStages.label: Sapling
growthStages.summary: Invests heavily in deep taproots before accelerating canopy height.

growthStages.label: Pole Crown
growthStages.summary: Sturdy horizontal limbs build a broad wind-resilient dome.

growthStages.label: Mast Years
growthStages.summary: Wind-pollinated flowers form nutrient-rich acorns in bumper mast cycles.

growthStages.label: Old Growth
growthStages.summary: Centuries-old crown anchors farm carbon, shade, and wildlife.

idealConditions.soilType: Deep, well-drained upland loam
idealConditions.daysToHarvest: 20–30 years to heavy acorn mast (300+ yr lifespan)

funFacts: White oaks support over 500 species of native butterflies and moths—vital chick food for nesting songbirds.
White oak heartwood is naturally watertight (packed with tyloses), making it prized for cooperage and shipbuilding.
A single mature white oak can transpire up to 400 liters of water on a hot July day, naturally air-conditioning the farmyard.

benefits.shade: Spreads 18–25 m wide, cooling farm roofs and pasture borders by 4–7 °C on summer afternoons.
benefits.soilHealth: Deep mycorrhizal roots recycle calcium and phosphorus while fallen leaves build dark humus.
benefits.pollinators: Spring catkins feed early bees; oak crowns shelter hundreds of insectivorous birds.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~28–36 kg CO₂/year sequestered by a mature tree

treeDetails.leafShape: 7–9 rounded finger-like lobes with smooth margins

nutritionHighlights: Low-tannin sweet acorns were historically leached and ground into nutritious flour; vital wildlife mast.
nasaMonitoring: NASA GEDI spaceborne LiDAR on the ISS measures oak canopy height and carbon biomass, while MODIS tracks autumn leaf senescence.

name: Mixed Temperate Forest
description: The misty forested hills behind the valley filter rainwater into farm springs, slow downslope storm runoff, and buffer wind across the valley floor.

growthStages.label: Understory Seed
growthStages.summary: Shade-tolerant maple, oak, and pine seeds germinate in damp duff.

growthStages.label: Regeneration
growthStages.summary: Young saplings compete for sunlit canopy gaps.

growthStages.label: Canopy Closure
growthStages.summary: Multi-layered crowns trap mist and build deep forest sponge soil.

growthStages.label: Seed Rain
growthStages.summary: Alternating pollen, cones, and winged samaras sustain wildlife.

growthStages.label: Climax Forest
growthStages.summary: Stable multi-age watershed protects valley microclimate.

idealConditions.soilType: Forest mull loam over fractured ridge bedrock

funFacts: Morning valley mist visible in the hills adds 'occult precipitation' as tree needles comb moisture straight from fog.
Intact ridge forests cut peak downstream flood surges by up to 60% compared to cleared slopes.
Underground fungal networks connect roots across tree species to share water during dry spells.

benefits.shade: Multi-layered canopy cools mountain air, generating gentle afternoon valley breezes.
benefits.soilHealth: Sponge-like leaf litter absorbs heavy rain and prevents hillside erosion.
benefits.pollinators: Early spring understory redbuds and serviceberries feed bees before crops bloom.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~7,500 kg CO₂/hectare/year net forest carbon sink

treeDetails.leafShape: Mix of lobed broadleaf oak/maple leaves and evergreen pine needles

nutritionHighlights: Watershed ecosystem supporting clean groundwater, wild berries, mushrooms, and maple sap.
nasaMonitoring: Landsat, MODIS EVI, and EONET fire alerts continuously monitor forest canopy health and wildfire smoke risk.

name: Red Maple
description: True to its name, red maple shows scarlet buds in late winter, crimson flowers in early spring, red leaf stems all summer, and blazing crimson foliage each autumn.

growthStages.label: Samara
growthStages.summary: Winged 'helicopter' samaras spin into moist pasture edges and sprout quickly.

growthStages.label: Seedling
growthStages.summary: Fast-growing shoots adapt to both damp lowlands and upland slopes.

growthStages.label: Mid Canopy
growthStages.summary: Oval symmetrical crown creates dappled pasture shade.

growthStages.label: Early Bloom
growthStages.summary: Tiny red blossoms open weeks before leaves, giving bees vital early nectar.

growthStages.label: Autumn Blaze
growthStages.summary: Brilliant scarlet leaves drop to nourish hedgerow soil.

idealConditions.soilType: Slightly acidic moist loam (very adaptable)

funFacts: Red maple is the most abundant native tree across eastern North America thanks to its adaptability.
Its red blooms are one of the very first nectar sources for honeybees emerging from winter.
While Sugar Maple is most famous for syrup, Red Maple sap can also be boiled into sweet syrup.

benefits.shade: Dense oval crown provides cool resting islands along middle-distance pasture fences.
benefits.soilHealth: Fast-decaying leaf litter builds topsoil nitrogen and moisture retention.
benefits.pollinators: Crucial March pollen & nectar bridge before orchard fruit trees blossom.

treeDetails.leafShape: 3–5 sharply toothed lobes with V-shaped sinuses and red petioles

nutritionHighlights: Produces sweet spring sap and winged samaras eaten by squirrels and finches.
nasaMonitoring: MODIS land-surface phenology satellites track spring green-up and autumn peak foliage across temperate hedgerows.

name: Sugar Maple
description: Standing alone in the sunlit meadow, this Sugar Maple shades grazing cattle from midday heat and relies on freeze-thaw spring cycles to pump sweet sap through its trunk.

growthStages.label: Samara
growthStages.summary: U-shaped winged samaras chill under winter snow before sprouting.

growthStages.label: Sapling
growthStages.summary: Shade-tolerant young stems steadily climb toward full sun.

growthStages.label: Open Crown
growthStages.summary: Forms a dense golden-green umbrella across the open meadow.

growthStages.label: Spring Sap
growthStages.summary: Freeze-thaw nights (<0°C) and sunny days (>5°C) drive sap flow.

growthStages.label: Mature Giant
growthStages.summary: Tappable trunks yield sweet syrup while shading grazing livestock.

idealConditions.soilType: Deep, fertile, calcium-rich moist loam

funFacts: It takes roughly 40 liters of Sugar Maple sap to boil down just 1 liter of pure maple syrup.
Sap flows only when night temperatures freeze below 0°C followed by sunny days above 4°C.
A lone pasture maple tree drops surface ground temperatures underneath by up to 8°C for resting cows.

benefits.shade: Expansive crown lowers pasture heat stress for cattle during peak July afternoons.
benefits.soilHealth: Hydraulic lift pulls moisture from deep subsoil up to shallow pasture grass roots overnight.
benefits.pollinators: Yellow-green spring flower tassels feed bees and hoverflies.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~26–30 kg CO₂/year per mature open-grown tree

treeDetails.leafShape: Classic 5-lobed palmate leaf with smooth U-shaped notches

nutritionHighlights: Maple syrup supplies natural manganese, riboflavin, zinc, and antioxidant polyphenols.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER freeze-thaw daily T2M_MIN/T2M_MAX cycles directly model spring maple sap run windows.

name: Pasture Grass & Clover
description: A living green carpet mixing deep-rooted cool-season tall fescue with nitrogen-fixing white clover. Clover pulls nitrogen from the air to naturally feed surrounding grasses without synthetic fertilizer.

growthStages.label: Over-seeding
growthStages.summary: Frost-seeding scatters clover seed into thawing pasture sod.

growthStages.label: Tillering
growthStages.summary: Grass blades thicken and clover stolons creep across bare patches.

growthStages.label: Lush Forage
growthStages.summary: Peak protein pasture growth supports rotational cattle grazing.

growthStages.label: Clover Bloom
growthStages.summary: Creamy white clover pom-poms blanket the field in bee forage.

growthStages.label: Hay / Grazing
growthStages.summary: Rotational grazing leaves 10 cm stubble so roots rebound rapidly.

idealConditions.soilType: Moist clay loam or silt loam

funFacts: White clover roots host Rhizobium bacteria that fix 80–140 kg of nitrogen per hectare from thin air.
Healthy rotational pastures infiltrate heavy thunderstorm rain up to 4x faster than bare plowed soil.
Deep grass roots store more carbon underground than many cultivated annual crops.

benefits.shade: Cool green turf reflects solar radiation and keeps topsoil 6–10 °C cooler than bare dirt.
benefits.soilHealth: Continuous living roots build soil organic matter and earthworm populations.
benefits.pollinators: White clover blooms rank among the top honeybee nectar plants on Earth.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~1,800–3,200 kg CO₂/ha stored in deep perennial root humus

nutritionHighlights: Balanced digestible energy and 16–22% crude protein forage supporting healthy pasture-raised dairy.
nasaMonitoring: MODIS NDVI and NASA SMAP topsoil moisture track pasture greenness and drought recovery across grazing valleys.

name: White Wildflowers (Yarrow & Wild Carrot)
description: Flat-topped lacy white umbels of yarrow and Queen Anne's lace form vital field-margin insectaries, hosting predatory wasps, ladybugs, and native bees right beside farm crops.

growthStages.label: Overwinter
growthStages.summary: Tiny dry seeds ride wind and winter chill along undisturbed fence margins.

growthStages.label: Basal Rosette
growthStages.summary: Feathery fern-like foliage spreads close to the ground.

growthStages.label: Bolting
growthStages.summary: Slender ridged stems lift buds above surrounding grasses.

growthStages.label: Lacy Umbels
growthStages.summary: Hundreds of tiny white florets create landing pads for beneficial insects.

growthStages.label: Seed Head
growthStages.summary: Cupped dry umbels curl inward to shelter birds and reseed margins.

idealConditions.soilType: Adaptable lean to loamy meadow soil

funFacts: Flat white umbels act as landing platforms for beneficial hoverflies and lacewings whose larvae eat crop aphids.
Yarrow leaves have been used for millennia in herbal poultices—its genus Achillea honors Achilles.
Look at the center of Queen Anne's lace: a single dark purple floret often sits right in the middle to lure pollinators.

benefits.shade: Fine feathery foliage shelters ground beetles and spiders along fence lines.
benefits.soilHealth: Deep rhizomes break up compacted fence-row edges and accumulate potassium & copper.
benefits.pollinators: Sustainably feeds butterflies, solitary bees, and aphid-hunting hoverflies all summer.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~900 kg CO₂/ha undisturbed meadow margin biomass

producingCountries: Widespread across Europe, North America, and temperate Asia
nutritionHighlights: Wild carrot is the direct ancestor of cultivated garden carrots; yarrow is a bitter aromatic herb (not livestock forage).
nasaMonitoring: Sentinel/Landsat multi-spectral imagery identifies flowering buffer strips that boost adjacent crop pollination.

name: Grazing Dairy Cattle
origin: Fertile Crescent (~10,500 years ago); rotational valley dairy
description: Pasture-raised cattle convert cellulose-rich meadow grass and clover into milk and nutrient-dense manure, cycling organic fertility back into the valley soil when rotated regularly.

growthStages.label: Spring Turnout
growthStages.summary: Herd enters fresh spring paddocks once grass reaches 15–20 cm.

growthStages.label: Peak Grazing
growthStages.summary: High-protein lush clover-grass forage fuels peak spring milk yield.

growthStages.label: Heat Shade
growthStages.summary: Cattle rest beneath the Sugar Maple when heat-humidity index climbs.

growthStages.label: Autumn Strip
growthStages.summary: Strip grazing stockpiled fescue extends fresh pasture before frost.

growthStages.label: Winter Hay
growthStages.summary: Herd transitions to summer-baled hay & corn silage under barn shelter.

idealConditions.soilType: Well-drained pasture loam (prevents winter mud)
idealConditions.daysToHarvest: Daily milk yield; 28-day paddock rest cycle

funFacts: Cattle heat stress begins around 25°C (Temperature-Humidity Index ≥ 72)—shade trees like Sugar Maple protect both welfare and milk yield.
A single cow consumes 50–90 liters of water and ~14 kg of dry pasture forage every day.
Well-managed rotational grazing mimics wild bison herds, building dark carbon-rich prairie soil.
uses: Natural compost & organic pasture manure cycling

benefits.shade: Relies directly on valley trees (Sugar Maple & Oak) to avoid afternoon thermal stress.
benefits.soilHealth: Rotational hoof impact and manure recycle phosphorus, nitrogen, and microbes into topsoil.
benefits.pollinators: Rotational rest paddocks allow clover and wildflowers to bloom between grazings.
benefits.co2PerYear: Rotational grazing helps pasture soils sequester ~1.5–2.5 t CO₂/ha/yr (offsetting livestock footprint)

nutritionHighlights: Grass-fed dairy supplies higher levels of omega-3 fatty acids, CLA, calcium, and vitamin K2.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER temperature + relative humidity (T2M + RH2M) calculate Livestock Heat-Stress Index, while MODIS tracks pasture biomass.

name: Rooftop Solar & NASA Sunlight
description: Mounted on the farmhouse roof, these solar panels harvest the exact same incoming shortwave sunlight (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN) that powers crop photosynthesis across the valley.

growthStages.label: Dawn Light
growthStages.summary: Diffuse morning sun wakes panels as valley mist burns off.

growthStages.label: Morning Ramp
growthStages.summary: Solar irradiance climbs past 500 W/m²; irrigation pumps run free.

growthStages.label: Solar Noon
growthStages.summary: Peak sunlight charges farm batteries and powers barn cooling.

growthStages.label: Afternoon Dip
growthStages.summary: Warm sun lingers across west hills while crops finish carbon uptake.

growthStages.label: Daily Yield
growthStages.summary: NASA CERES tracks net daily solar energy reaching the farm.

idealConditions.soilType: South-facing 30° pitched farmhouse roof
idealConditions.daysToHarvest: Instantaneous daily kWh electricity + photosynthesis energy

funFacts: Solar panels actually generate electricity MORE efficiently on crisp sunny spring mornings than on 38°C heatwave afternoons.
NASA CERES satellites measure top-of-atmosphere vs. surface sunlight every day across the entire globe.
A 10 kW farmhouse roof array offsets ~11,000 kg of CO₂ per year while powering drip irrigation and cold storage.
uses: Cold storage for harvested apples & tomatoes

benefits.shade: Shades the red farmhouse roof, lowering attic heat gain during July heatwaves.
benefits.soilHealth: Powers precision low-pressure drip pumps that cut soil erosion and water waste.
benefits.pollinators: Solar farm margins planted with clover and yarrow double as pollinator corridors.
benefits.co2PerYear: ~10,500 kg CO₂/year avoided grid emissions (10 kW farmhouse array)

producingCountries: Global Open NASA POWER Coverage (0.5° × 0.5° Grid)
nutritionHighlights: Solar photons drive 100% of crop photosynthesis (PAR) and clean farm irrigation power.
nasaMonitoring: NASA POWER ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN (CERES FLASHFlux) delivers daily surface solar irradiance in kWh/m²/day for any field on Earth.
